STEP 1 - Scene: A single half of a cooked yellow corn cob (corn on the cob, cut crosswise) on a white square plate. Photographed from directly above (top-down view).

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white plate is a square dinner-style plate, roughly 24 cm across. Plate area ≈ 24 x 24 ≈ 576 cm^2 (using the square outline; a round-equivalent of ~26 cm gives a similar result).

STEP 3 - Items: One piece of corn (sweet corn kernels, cob segment cut crosswise). No visible butter, oil, or sauce.

STEP 4 - Area: The corn disc is about 4.5 cm in diameter, so its top face is roughly 16 cm^2, about 3% of the plate. Food covers only ~3% of the plate.

STEP 5 - Volume: The cob piece is a short cylinder about 3.5 cm tall, so the gross volume is about 16 cm^2 x 3.5 cm ≈ 56 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Corn pieces with cob are fairly airy and mostly kernels plus cob. Using a bulk density of about 0.6 g/ml for cut vegetable pieces gives ≈ 34 g. A whole cob segment is dense on its own, but the cob core is inedible and is counted here as part of the plated weight, so this stays within a reasonable range.

STEP 7 - Energy: Sweet corn, cooked, ≈ 96 kcal per 100 g. 34 g x 0.96 ≈ 33 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A half cob of corn is a small side portion, typically 30–60 g with the cob. About 34 g and 33 kcal is plausible for what is visible, with no other food on the plate.
